title: The War of the Egg End
lines: The emperor of Lilliput, Golbasto Momaren Evlame Gurdilo Shefin Mully Ully Gue, was a monarch of breathtaking vanity. His imperial majesty stood just barely taller than the nail of my little finger.

I knelt before him — or rather, I lowered my head as one might bow to a particularly short child — and swore an oath of allegiance. In return, he granted me the title of Nardac, the highest honor in the realm.

My first use of Lilliputian politics came when the emperor asked for my help against the empire of Blefuscu, the great rival across the channel. The two nations had been at war for generations over the proper way to break an egg.

The controversy was this: the emperor's great-grandfather had cut his finger while breaking an egg at the larger end. He decreed that all eggs henceforth be broken at the smaller end. The Blefuscudians refused, calling this heresy against the sacred traditions of the egg.

Eleven thousand Lilliputians had already died in the Great Egg War. The Blefuscudian fleet — fifty warships — was anchored just across the channel, preparing for invasion. The emperor looked at me meaningfully.

I waded into the channel — the water barely reached my waist — and, using cables I had twisted from Lilliputian ropes, I tied all fifty Blefuscudian ships together and dragged them back to the Lilliputian harbor. The war was over.
